investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T18:02–18:10Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle checks required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no existing pod can be evicted to free capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a remote state, causing a total contract gap for all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie pods have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no schedulable capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had their labels changed or the pod spec's node selector may have been tightened, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — eval probe resource leak: prior eval runs that did not clean up remote agent pods (via withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity for concurrent eval and production workloads, requiring node pool scaling.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place any new kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~144–147 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks impossible. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval runner or application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval environment.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes do not match the pod's required node selector, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes' VM quota is undersized for concurrent eval runs, exhaustion will recur.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 18:05 and 18:10 UTC on 2026-07-06 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching pod affinity/selector. The eval pod could not be scheduled, so no agent was ever created, and the expected-output contract received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and the remaining 2 have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption was also unable to help (no preemption victims found). As a result, every eval pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing no agent and no evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata peer-pods node pool; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T18:02–18:10Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle checks required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no existing pod can be evicted to free capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never obtained a VM ID or a remote state, causing a total contract gap for all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie pods have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no schedulable capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had their labels changed or the pod spec's node selector may have been tightened, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — eval probe resource leak: prior eval runs that did not clean up remote agent pods (via withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity for concurrent eval and production workloads, requiring node pool scaling.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place any new kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~144–147 s), preventing agent creation and making all downstream state-polling and runtime checks impossible. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an eval runner or application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval environment.

If the pod's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that it excludes all 6 nodes regardless of VM capacity, the primary cause shifts from resource exhaustion to affinity misconfiguration.

If a passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime is observed in the run history (lastPassingAt is currently null with previousRunCount=0), it would indicate this is a first-run or newly introduced failure rather than a regression from a previously passing state.

If user-traffic or incident signals surface showing real agent provisioning succeeding for end users during this window, the failure would be scoped entirely to the eval probe's service account or namespace rather than the shared production scheduling pool.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., via the Kubernetes API or a metrics endpoint) and alerts when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, before agent creation is attempted.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agent eval suite that verifies at least one schedulable node exists for the kata peer-pod class before invoking createAgent, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct failure mode rather than a timeout.

Introduce a historical run baseline for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime so that regressions from a passing state can be detected automatically (currently previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null).

Add a sibling-correlation eval that fires when all checks within the remote-agents feature fail simultaneously with the same scheduling message, to distinguish infrastructure-wide capacity failures from per-check application bugs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 18:05 and 18:10 UTC on 2026-07-06 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching pod affinity/selector. The eval pod could not be scheduled, so no agent was ever created, and the expected-output contract received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector at all, and the remaining 2 have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption was also unable to help (no preemption victims found). As a result, every eval pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing no agent and no evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata peer-pods node pool; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — the pod must schedule before any evidence can be collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, so this specific check does not gate a declared outage on its own, but all three failing together indicates a shared scheduling dependency.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 affinity-matching nodes — concurrent workloads or a prior eval run may have exhausted the finite peer-pod VM quota, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

[Likely] The node pool for remote agents has shrunk or one of the two affinity-matching nodes became NotReady/cordoned, reducing available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed to schedule a single eval pod.

[Possible] The pod's node affinity/selector is overly restrictive, targeting only 2 of 6 nodes, meaning any capacity pressure on those 2 nodes immediately causes Unschedulable failures with no fallback.
[Possible] A prior eval run's cleanup did not release kata.peerpods.io/vm resources (e.g., a leaked peer-pod VM), reducing available slots for subsequent runs.
[Lower likelihood] A cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm was recently tightened, reducing the number of schedulable slots available to the eval namespace.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the 2 affinity-matching nodes to determine current slot availability and identify any pods holding slots that should have been released.

Check for leaked or stuck remote-agent eval pods from prior runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916), as these would hold kata.peerpods.io/vm slots indefinitely.
If resource exhaustion is confirmed, assess whether the kata peer-pods node pool needs additional nodes or increased kata.peerpods.io/vm quota to support concurrent eval runs without contention.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on the remote-agent pod spec to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional and whether additional nodes could be made eligible to increase scheduling resilience.

Monitor the remote-agents feature health status: with remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state (both required=true) failing, the feature is at or past the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold and approaching outageAfterFailures=2 per infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188.

After resolving the scheduling issue, re-run all three remote-agents checks to confirm recovery and verify that the expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is fully populated and the 'hello from aura' assertion passes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted on the affinity-matching nodes, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota, or affinity misconfiguration) must be investigated.

If the eval pod spec shows a node affinity/selector that does not match any currently Ready node (i.e., the label was removed or changed), the cause is a configuration drift in node labels rather than resource exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and schedules without error, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released its slots) rather than a sustained capacity problem.
If only remote-agent checks fail while local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also fail with the same scheduler message, the problem may be broader than the kata peer-pods pool.
If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources at the time of investigation, the failure may have been caused by a node going NotReady rather than resource exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability on the affinity-matching nodes before attempting agent creation, so scheduling exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout in the agent creation flow.
Add a check that detects and alerts on leaked remote-agent eval pods (pods in Running or Pending state beyond a maximum expected lifetime) to prevent slot exhaustion from prior runs.
Add a historical baseline eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization over time so capacity trends can be detected before exhaustion occurs.

Consider a pre-flight scheduling dry-run eval (kubectl --dry-run=server) that validates a remote-agent pod would be schedulable before the full agent creation probe runs, enabling faster and cheaper detection of scheduling failures.
